system_prompt:
You are a medical pathology simplification assistant. Convert the following surgical pathology diagnostic report into simple, plain English that a patient and their family can understand (at a 6th-grade reading level).

=== EXTRACTED CLINICAL ENTITIES — YOU MUST RETAIN ALL OF THESE ===
Specimen: Prostate; Radical prostatectomy; weight 50.0g; dimensions 5.1 x 4.3 x 3.2 cm
  Associated structure: bilateral dorsally attached seminal vesicles
  Associated structure: ductus deferentes
Histologic diagnosis: Acinar adenocarcinoma (bilateral)
  ICD-O-3: 8140/3
Gleason Score: 4 + 3 = 7 (7b) | ISUP Grade Group: 3 | High-grade pattern: 60%
Invasion status: Perineural invasion: present; Lymphovascular invasion: absent; Extracapsular extension: absent; Seminal vesicle invasion: absent
Resection status: R0
  Margin — apical margin, right: negative
  Margin — apical margin, left: negative
  Margin — basal margin, right: negative
  Margin — basal margin, left: negative
  Margin — vas deferens margin, right: negative
  Margin — vas deferens margin, left: negative
Additional finding: Residual prostate with adenomyomatosis
Additional finding: Additional examinations for verification will be carried out
=================================================================
CRITICAL RETENTION RULE: Every entity, value, measurement, date, medication name, finding, and recommendation listed above MUST appear in your simplified output. Do not omit any of them.

Rules:
1. Explain what tissue or organ was examined (e.g. prostate specimen removed during surgery).
2. Keep essential medical terms but immediately explain each in parentheses on first use, e.g. 'adenocarcinoma (a cancer that starts in the gland cells of an organ)'.
3. Explain the cancer type, whether it is localized or spreading, and the grade in plain words:
   - Explain Gleason score simply: e.g. 'Gleason score 7 (a grading system from 6 to 10 that shows how abnormal the cells look; 7 means moderately aggressive cells)'.
   - Explain surgical margins simply: e.g. 'resection margins (the outer cut edge of the tissue removed by the surgeon; clear/R0 margins mean no cancer cells were touching the edge)'.
   - Explain IHC stains simply: e.g. 'immunohistochemistry (special chemical dye tests that identify specific proteins in cancer cells)'.
4. Preserve all measurements (weights, dimensions in cm or mm, percentages) accurately. Never fabricate or omit numbers.
5. Write as continuous plain prose paragraphs without bullet points or headers.
6. Maintain a calm, objective, and supportive tone. Do not provide speculative prognoses or medical advice beyond what is written in the report.
7. Output only the simplified text, nothing else.
8. CRITICAL — ENTITY RETENTION: Every entity listed in the extracted entities block above MUST appear in your simplified output — including specimen weight, dimensions, Gleason score primary + secondary + total + ISUP Grade Group, percentage of high-grade pattern, every margin location and its status, every IHC marker and its result, and invasion findings. Do not omit any of them.
user_prompt:
--- Your Task ---
Please simplify the following surgical pathology report into plain English that a patient can understand:

Original Medical Report:
Material submitted: Prostate.
Clinical data: Known prostate carcinoma.


Pathological-anatomical report:

Macroscopic:
A prostatectomy specimen weighing 50 g and measuring 5.1 x 4.3 x 3.2 cm with bds. dorsally attached seminal vesicles and ductus deferentes. Seminal vesicle on the right measuring up to 3.5 cm, on the left up to 2.5 cm. Ductus deferens on the right up to 6 cm, ductus deferens on the left up to 5.5 cm.  Color marking of the prostate ventrally blue and dorsally black.
1st apical margin, right in (A, B), left in (C, D). (4 Bl, kR).
2. base of vesicle, right (A, B), left (C, D) (4 Bl, kR).
3. sedimentation margins of vas deferens, right (A), left (B). (2 Bl, kR).
4. lamellation of the prostate. The cut surface, grayish-beige, firm-elastic, fibrous, partially cystic. Embedding in toto, right half of prostate from apical to basal in (A - U ), left half from apical to basal in (V-Z19) ( 45 Bl, kR).
5. embedding of the seminal vesicles: Transition of the prostate into the right seminal vesicle in (A+B), seminal vesicle right lamellar in (C-F).  Transition of the prostate into the left seminal vesicle in (G+H), seminal vesicle lamellated in (I-L) (12 Bl, kR).

Microscopically:
1. fibromuscular tissue with localized prostate glands. No inflammatory infiltrates. In the right-sided area a microfocal area of abnormally positioned glands with partly prominent nucleoli. Basal cell layer not recognizable.
2. fibromuscular tissue with localized prostate glands (more on the left than on the right). No cytomorphologic atypia.
3. wall parts of the ductus deferentes with locotypical structure. No inflammation or atypia.

 - b.w. -


4. infiltrates of the tumor described above are visible on both sides of the prostate (more on the right than on the left). In addition to a single-gland structure, confluent growth patterns are also visible. There is an ingrowth into perineural sheaths. The ink-marked margins of the specimen are not reached. No overgrowth of the prostate tissue or infiltration into the seminal vesicle is visible. Residual prostate with an implied nodular structure. No inflammatory infiltrates.
5. seminal vesicles on both sides with locotypical structure. No inflammation or atypia.

Tumor blocks for extra examinations: 4A, 4C, 4Z2.

Assessment:
1st-5th prostatectomy specimen with bilateral infiltrates of acinar adenocarcinoma, perineural sheath infiltration. Tumor-free apical and basal sedimentation lines. Tumor-free seminal vesicles on both sides. Tumor-free ductus deferens deposits on both sides. Residual prostate with adenomyomatosis.

TNM classification (Prostate 2017, 8th edition): pT2c, pN0 (0/12 taking into account parallel submission), L0, V0, Pn1, R0;

Gleason score: 4 + 3 = 7b (60%4 proportion, 40%3 proportion).

Gleason pattern Gleason score ISUP graduation group Applies
= 3 + 3 = 6 1
3 + 4 7a 2
4 + 3 7b 3 X
4 + 4 8 4
4 + 5, 5 + 4, 5 + 5 9-10 5


ICD-O-3 Explanation Applies
8140/3 Adenocarcinoma n.d. X
8020/3 Undifferentiated carcinoma n.a.

We will carry out additional examinations for verification and report back.

output_text:
This report describes your prostate, which was removed during surgery (a radical prostatectomy). The removed prostate weighed 50.0 grams and measured 5.1 by 4.3 by 3.2 centimeters. Along with the prostate, the two seminal vesicles (small glands that help make semen) and the tubes called ductus deferentes (also known as vas deferens, which carry sperm) were also removed.

The main finding from looking at the tissue under the microscope is acinar adenocarcinoma (a type of cancer that starts in the gland cells). This cancer was found on both sides of your prostate. The specific code for this type of cancer is 8140/3.

The cancer was graded using a system called the Gleason score. Your score is 4 + 3 = 7 (also noted as 7b). This means the cancer cells look moderately aggressive. The ISUP Grade Group is 3. About 60% of the cancer had the more aggressive pattern (Gleason pattern 4).

The cancer was found to be growing along some small nerves (this is called perineural invasion). However, it was not found to be growing into blood vessels or lymphatic channels (lymphovascular invasion was absent). The cancer did not grow outside the prostate capsule (extracapsular extension was absent), and it also did not spread into the seminal vesicles (seminal vesicle invasion was absent).

The surgery successfully removed all the visible cancer. This is called an R0 resection, meaning no cancer cells were found at the edges of the removed tissue (resection margins). Specifically, the right apical margin, left apical margin, right basal margin, left basal margin, right vas deferens margin, and left vas deferens margin were all negative, meaning no cancer cells were touching these edges.

The remaining prostate tissue also showed a condition called adenomyomatosis (a non-cancerous change where there's an overgrowth of glands and muscle tissue). Additional examinations for verification will be carried out, and you will receive an update.
